ranking.note: Raised to P2: same class of harm as #35837 (RPC silently returns a wrong 'not found' answer); placed last in the band because the trigger is rarer.
Moved up: breaks TCP backpressure and hangs on macOS, belongs with the other HTTP-server correctness bugs rather than mid-list features.
Moved up: an operator silently shown 'no warnings' is a wrong-output bug, ranked with the other output-correctness fixes.
Moved up: user-visible 'Internal bug detected' for miners on shutdown is a concrete bug, ahead of new diagnostic fields.
Moved up: emitted schema defaults that fail validators break downstream tooling now and are milestoned for backport.
Moved down: a new method with only partially demonstrated demand ranks below the output-correctness fixes, per this category's rule on new methods.
Moved up: warning prevents silent key reuse across multipath branches, a privacy consequence stronger than the other new fields.
Moved down: monitoring feature with an old issue behind it, but no caller is currently broken by its absence.
Moved down: useful new control surface for pruned nodes, but no external consumer is blocked today.
Moved up: removes a real pruned-node/txindex incompatibility and gives callers structured recovery data, more than a convenience field.
Raised to P3 and moved up: same problem as #34038, which was P3; competing approaches must share a band since the pending design decision is what blocks both.
Moved down: a read-only diagnostic field in getpeerinfo, ranked with the other such fields.
Moved down: diagnostic-only getpeerinfo field with no external consumer asking, grouped with #27052.
Moved down: REST parity for an existing RPC, no caller blocked, so it sits with the other convenience additions.
Moved up: named external generators (corepc, btcd) currently hardcode the mapping, a documented consumer request.
Moved down: benefit is developer/regtest tooling only, below interface gaps affecting production callers.
Moved down: wallet-first change; its rpc relevance is limited to error-message wording.
Lowered to P4: internal encapsulation refactor with no bug or user-visible payoff, same class as #36198.
Lowered to P4: internal logging/test tidy-up in the HTTP server, consistent with the other no-user-impact refactors.
Lowered to P4: pure functional-test addition, same category of work as #35893 which was P4.

inconsistencies: #34038, #35387 and #35355 all rework trace-logging configuration and the logging RPC surface; #34038 carries an Approach NACK pointing at #35387. They must be banded together and reviewed as one decision: settle #34038 vs #35387 first, then #35355, which folds the same interface change into an atomics rewrite.

Large HTTP-server cluster touching the same files: #36187, #36200, #36204, #36259, #35780, #36276, #36159, #36124, #36198. Merge order matters; #36276 is an explicit follow-up to already-merged #36123, and #36124 is a follow-up to #35829.

#35780 and #36276 both fix cases where the HTTP server drops or mishandles client data and both are blamed for intermittent CI failures; I split them (P2 vs P3) only because #35780 costs Windows clients the actual error reply while #36276's exposure is capped at 65kB.
#35837 and #35728 solve the same shape of problem (an RPC reporting 'nothing there' when the truth is 'we could not read it'); they should be banded alike and reviewed as a pair.
#36297 and #36175 both change getopenrpcinfo output; #36297 fixes defaults that make the schema invalid today and should be reviewed first, since #36175 extends the same schema.
#27052 and #31672 both add a diagnostic field to getpeerinfo plus netinfo plumbing; reviewing them together avoids duplicated discussion about which internal counters belong in that result.
#35893 and #36261 are both test-only additions to existing RPC coverage and were previously split across P4 and P3 without a difference in consequence.
#29278 (wallet -maxfeerate) is wallet-first by the category rules; its presence here rests only on the error text returned by broadcast RPCs.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: one interface-security fix (#36187), a small P2 group of HTTP-server availability/correctness bugs plus the two RPCs that return silently wrong answers, a long P3 tail of genuine interface gaps and small bugs, and a P4 tail of internal refactors, tests and doc touch-ups. New methods and new diagnostic fields with no named external consumer were kept below the output-correctness fixes, per this category's rule.
